decisions.decision: A data file containing even one ticket with an invalid `due` value is rejected at load with an error naming the record, even with `DUE_TIMES` off.
decisions.alternative: The service could start, flag the affected record for repair, and continue serving the other tickets.

decisions.decision: Backfill uses the priority stored on the ticket at migration time, including for tickets whose priority changed after creation.
decisions.alternative: Backfill could recover the ticket's original priority from its creation audit entry and use that priority to assign the deadline.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:43 (R-6, backfill calculation); record/01-intake.md:81 (Q2, startup behaviour)

decisions.decision: Operators are to deploy with `DUE_TIMES` off, check that the production data file contains the due times, and then switch it on.
decisions.alternative: The service could verify on startup that the file already contains every due time before honoring `DUE_TIMES=on`.

decisions.decision: An explicitly empty `DUE_HOURS_*` setting selects the default for that priority.
decisions.alternative: An explicitly empty setting could fail startup so an empty deployment variable cannot silently assign tickets the default deadline.

decisions.decision: When `overdue=true`, `status`, and `priority` are supplied together, an overdue ticket qualifies if it matches at least one of the requested status and priority.
decisions.alternative: With the overdue filter active, clients could expect a ticket to match all three criteria, as the API documentation describes for combined filters.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:39 (R-5, Combination); repo/docs/api.md:76 (existing documented filter semantics)

decisions.decision: Requester notifications keep their current content and triggers when due times are enabled.
decisions.alternative: The ticket receipt could tell the requester the promised response deadline.

decisions.decision: The API represents `due` as an ISO 8601 UTC string in the same format as `created`.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have intended a numeric Unix timestamp for clients to compare directly.

decisions.decision: The ticket creation audit entry records only title, priority, requester, and status, even when due times are enabled.
decisions.alternative: The creation audit entry could also record the deadline originally assigned to the ticket.

decisions.decision: The weekly report and its dashboard data retain the existing ticket counts by status and priority when due times are enabled.
decisions.alternative: The weekly report and dashboard could also give support leads a count of overdue tickets.

decisions.decision: The operator CLI keeps its current commands and output when due times are enabled.
decisions.alternative: Operators could see the deadline in `tickets show` and the human-readable `tickets list` while scripts keep using the existing raw columns.
decisions.where: record/01-intake.md:114 (Q6, lines 114–121); repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:48 (R-6, CLI and report)

decisions.decision: Overdue results use the existing cursor pagination and ticket ID order, with the overdue filter applied before paging.
decisions.alternative: The overdue view could return the full work queue at once, ordered by earliest deadline first.

decisions.decision: A client that includes `due` in a ticket request body receives a 400 unknown-field error.
decisions.alternative: Clients could send back the `due` field they received, and the server could discard it while applying the permitted changes.

decisions.decision: Backfilling `due` preserves each ticket's existing `updated` timestamp.
decisions.alternative: The backfill could set `updated` to the migration time so consumers looking for recently changed tickets pick up the new deadline.

decisions.decision: The production JSON keeps format version 1 and stores `due` as an optional field on each ticket record.
decisions.alternative: The same version 1 file could store deadlines in a top-level map keyed by ticket ID so readers that require the original ticket fields can still read those records.

decisions.decision: The release that introduces due times is designated 1.5.0.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have intended to ship the feature as 1.4.1, the next patch release on the 1.4 line.
